# s377 — plan-parallel blocked names the right dependencies

**Findings:** s376 relay report 2026-10-18: no test covers an item with one dependency placed and one never placed; docs/agents.md says `blocked` lists dependencies "never placed", but a capped, unspecified or sibling-held item keeps its full pending list · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** changing which dependencies `blocked` reports, or the `next --batch --disjoint` shape it mirrors.

## Why

`plan_parallel` in `src/slicer/ops.py` builds `blocked` two ways. An item still in the pool after the last wave lists only the dependencies that never got a wave. An item the pool dropped (capped, unspecified, or held by a sibling worktree) keeps every pending dependency. No test pins the first case when only some dependencies were placed. The `plan-parallel` row in `docs/agents.md` describes only the first case, so a reader expects the narrower list for every item.

## Files

- `tests/test_plan_parallel.py`.
- `docs/agents.md` (the `plan-parallel` row's `blocked` sentence).

## Failing tests

- `test_PlanParallel_OneDependencyPlacedOneNot_WaitingOnNamesOnlyTheUnplaced`. It fails until the code is mutated to report the full pending list; it is a guard test, so watch it go red under that mutation instead of on a clean tree.

## Implement

1. Add the test. Item A depends on B (open, disjoint, placed in a wave) and on C (outside the pool, never placed). Assert that A is in `blocked` with `waiting_on == ["C"]` and in no wave.
2. Mutation-check: make the leftover branch report `pending` instead of `unmet` and watch the test go red, then revert.
3. Reword the `blocked` sentence in `docs/agents.md`: an item left over after the last wave lists only its never-placed dependencies; a capped, unspecified or sibling-held item lists every dependency it was waiting on, as `next --batch` does.
